name: a-burst-of-hovers-leaves-no-shadow-on-the-sidebar
description:
The hover URL card's widget resizes a round trip after the page inside it has already laid out, so while a burst of retargets is in flight the card is measured against a viewport that is one frame stale. The stack was anchored top-right inside a widget anchored to the pane's LEFT edge, which turned that lag into a sideways slide - and a card wider than the stale viewport reported a NEGATIVE offsetLeft, which the browser added to the widget's own origin and registered the drop shadow tens of pixels inside the sidebar, on a layer that spans the whole window.

What it measures: a rAF sampler inside the toast document records the card's own client rect on every frame of the burst. A card that slides out of its surface reports a left below zero, which is the exact reading that becomes a shadow on the sidebar. The sampler is armed before the burst and read after it, so no frame in between is skipped.

THE BURST IS THE POINT. Every existing hover scenario settles between pushes, which is exactly when the artefact is gone. These modifier flips run in one synchronous loop with no settle at all.

The three captures are artifacts for a person to look at, with no pixel assertion on them. A region_mean band over the sidebar was tried first and read byte-identical across all three, so it could not have told a ghost from a clean run either way.

actions.expression: (() => { const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = 'https://example.com/a/path/long/enough/to/outgrow/the/widget/before/it/has/resized/itself'; a.textContent = 'link'; a.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;left:0;top:0;width:100%;height:100%;z-index:99'; document.body.appendChild(a); return 'armed'; })()
actions.note: one link over the whole page, so the pointer never has to move again
REAL pointer move onto the link

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); const b = t.getBoundingClientRect(); return [Math.round(b.left), Math.round(b.width), Math.round(window.innerWidth)].join(':'); })()
actions.note: calibration, no assertion: the card's resting left, its width and the widget viewport it sits in

actions.expression: (() => { window.__burst = []; const tick = () => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast'); if (t) { const b = t.getBoundingClientRect(); window.__burst.push([Math.round(b.left), Math.round(b.width)]); } window.__burstRaf = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }; tick(); return 'sampling'; })()
actions.note: every frame from here to the reading below, so no intermediate layout is skipped

actions.expression: (() => { for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { window.atriumSetNavModifiers(false, i % 2 === 0, false); } return 'burst'; })()
actions.note: THE BURST: six flips in one synchronous loop, each one changing the hint, the URL's fit budget and so the card's width - with no round trip finishing between them

actions.expression: (() => { window.atriumSetNavModifiers(false, false, false); const h = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .cthint'); return h ? h.textContent : 'no hint'; })()

actions.note: THE CONTROL for the two absence readings below: a sampler that never ran would report a clean minimum

actions.expression: (() => { const min = Math.min.apply(null, window.__burst.map(f => f[0])); return min >= 0 ? 'inside' : 'slid ' + (-min) + 'px past its own start edge'; })()
actions.note: A card that slid out of its own surface reports a negative left, and that is the offset the shadow was registered at
calibration, no assertion: how many distinct widths the card wore across the burst

actions.expression: (() => { const t = document.querySelector('.toasts .toast .ctl'); return t && t.textContent ? 'card' : 'no card'; })()
actions.note: THE PRESENCE CONTROL: a run that dropped the card would satisfy the absence readings for the wrong reason

assertions.desc: the link the whole run hovers exists
the card came up before the burst
the per-frame sampler was installed before the burst, not after it
the six flips ran, so the readings below are of a burst and not of a resting card
the burst ended with no modifier held, so the card is back at its resting width
Presence control: the card is still up and still showing a URL after the burst
the card really left, so the last capture is of a sidebar with nothing on it

assertions.label: no-throw-in-the-burst
assertions.desc: a throw mid-push would leave the previous registration standing
THE CONTROL: the sampler really recorded the burst, so the reading below is of frames and not of an empty list
No frame of the burst put the card past its own start edge, which is the negative offset that became a shadow on the sidebar
